affectedPublicSurfaces: THE CONFIRMATION PAYLOAD'S DISCRIMINATOR — the surface of this slice. `proposed_change` is the verbatim tool arguments (`proposed_change=dict(block.arguments)` inside `WorkflowApprovalRequiredPayload(...)` — at `services/agent/runner/core.py:1538` in this tree, NOT the `:1510` the issue body cites) stored in uncapped JSONB (`models/models.py:689-739`) and bound by `params_sha` (`services/agent/runner/confirmation.py:130-158`), so a list of orders needs NO schema change. What it lacks is a SHAPE: nothing on the payload says whether a `proposed_change` is one listing field, one discount or a batch, so every reader guesses. This slice adds the typed discriminator and its `batch` variant. Note where the discriminator belongs: `services/agent/events/payloads.py` carries NO discriminant literal at all today — its own docstring says so — while the event-envelope discriminators live in the sibling `envelope.py` (`event_type: Literal[...]` at `envelope.py:55-90`, combined via `Field(discriminator="event_type")` at `:107`). Follow that established pattern rather than inventing a second discriminator style in a module that has none. EXISTING SINGLE-PROPOSAL PAYLOADS KEEP THEIR CURRENT SHAPE under their own discriminator and must render byte-identically — that compatibility is the release risk, not the new variant.

THE `batch` VARIANT ITSELF: confirmed orders GROUPED BY BUCKET in deadline order, each carrying its DEADLINE and the RUNG that deadline came from (#1797's `rts` / `tts` / collection / fallback ladder), plus every excluded order with its reason. #1803's re-verify and #1808's sheet both read this shape, so a field named loosely here is a field two slices are stuck with.

`packages/contracts/src/review.ts` — the TypeScript mirror, and a real cross-stack contract. Today the confirmation field is a SCALAR: `ReviewInputFieldDescriptor` carries `prefillValue: string` (`review.ts:15-23`) over the kinds `option-list | upload | free-text` (`review.ts:13`), which is exactly why the demo fakes the dispatch batch as the literal string `"Hàng đợi T5 — 6 đơn (chỉ đọc theo thứ hạng)"` (`apps/demo/src/lib/workflows/process-order/review.ts:28`, and again as `prefillValue` at `:70`). The mirrored discriminated union is the TYPE ONLY — the sheet that renders it is #1808. `@juli/contracts` is consumed by both demo and dashboard, so a breaking edit to `ReviewInputFieldDescriptor` breaks every existing review screen.

THE PARAMS HASH BINDING. `params_sha` must cover the CONFIRMED ORDER LIST, so the set the seller saw is exactly the set the run is bound to. Adding or removing one order changes the hash and the confirmation no longer matches — that is the mechanism by which #1803's executed set cannot silently widen, and it is a consent-integrity property (S-NFR-2), not a convenience.
STILL ONE CONFIRMATION, N = 1 (S-FR-3). No new confirmation surface, no second pause, no additional option. The whole batch is the single proposal.
NO schema change — `proposed_change` is existing uncapped JSONB. NO new HTTP route. NO rendering, NO re-verify, NO execution.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE IN THIS SLICE. `proposed_change` is already uncapped JSONB (`models/models.py:689-739`) holding the verbatim tool arguments, so a list of orders fits without touching Postgres. Do not open a migration file and do not open `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`; migration numbers are RESERVED BY META and never read from head, but the correct action here is not to reserve one — it is to not need one. Stable and candidate run the same schema, so a code rollback needs no downgrade. The compatibility risk is entirely at the PAYLOAD level and it is real: rows written before this slice carry no discriminator and must keep deserialising, and rows written after it must stay valid JSON for the previous release, which simply ignores the extra key. Persisting a window, a rung column or a dispatch ledger is #1799/#1805 work with its own reserved number.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. `proposed_change` stays shapeless, every reader keeps guessing, and the demo keeps faking the dispatch batch as the string at `apps/demo/src/lib/workflows/process-order/review.ts:28`. #1803 and #1808 stay blocked. Nothing about the deployed system changes and no seller sees anything different. A discriminator that breaks the single-proposal shape must never be merged to unblock the batch variant: every live confirmation in the product renders through that shape.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. NO DOWNGRADE IS NEEDED — there is no migration. Rows already written stay VALID JSON: the previous release reads `proposed_change` as an opaque dict and ignores an unrecognised discriminator key, so a batch payload written since cutover is inert rather than fatal to it. What the previous release CANNOT do is execute such a batch, so any run left paused on a batch confirmation must be allowed to EXPIRE on its 4 h window rather than resumed — it has no handler on the old code. The TypeScript mirror rolls back with the same deploy; a candidate demo build carrying the union against a backend that no longer emits it simply never sees the `batch` variant, which is a narrowing and not a crash. Nothing in either direction ships a package: this slice contains no write path.

doNotInfer: Do NOT write a migration. `proposed_change` is already uncapped JSONB; nothing here needs a column. Migration numbers are RESERVED BY META and never read from head.

Do NOT break the existing single-proposal payload shape. The discriminator is ADDITIVE; every confirmation live in the product today renders through that shape, and a row written before this slice must still deserialise.
Do NOT change `ReviewInputFieldDescriptor`'s existing fields or the `option-list | upload | free-text` kinds in a breaking way. `@juli/contracts` is consumed by apps/demo AND apps/dashboard.
Do NOT build UI. The `packages/contracts` change is the TYPE MIRROR ONLY; the sheet that renders the `batch` variant is #1808. One domain per issue.
Do NOT add a second confirmation, a second pause, or an option beyond N = 1 (S-FR-3). The whole batch is the single proposal.

Do NOT hand-author the TypeScript test's payload. Parse a payload the BACKEND actually serialised; a hand-written JSON literal proves only that the test author agrees with themselves. Bind the Python tests to the real serialiser and the real `params_sha` path, never to a `**kwargs` double.
Do NOT re-verify, execute, ship or register any tool here. That is #1803.

Do NOT recompute a deadline or a cutoff in the payload builder. Each order's deadline and its RUNG come from #1797's ladder; the documented cutoff is the last resort only, and a deadline without its rung is invalid.

Do NOT build a vendor-refusal branch or a field implying one. TikTok does NOT refuse a ship write during a pending cancellation (ADR-092 amendment 2026-09-05); a cancellation-pending order is HARD-EXCLUDED by Juli's own code and appears on the payload as an exclusion with its reason.

Do NOT add a cancel field, a cancel action or a cancel tool to the payload or the union. No cancel tool exists in this allowlist, ever. Do NOT add a Create Packages or Confirm Package Shipment variant: in SEA TikTok creates the package at order time, and Confirm Package Shipment is certified-warehouse-provider-only.
Do NOT model a superset. The payload's confirmed list is the CEILING for execution; #1803 may narrow it and may never widen it, and the params hash is what makes that enforceable.
Do NOT model FBT or Seller Own Fleet execution. Those orders appear only as EXCLUSIONS with their reasons; FBT is monitor-only by design and SOF is v2.
Do NOT let an order id, a window id or an internal enum reach a seller-facing string, and do NOT write English seller copy. Use the shared banned-pattern source both guards already read.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); apps/** and ios/** are on this epic's doNotLoad list — the only permitted cross-check on them is that `pnpm -w turbo run build` still passes.

Do NOT invent a second discriminator style. `services/agent/events/payloads.py` carries no discriminant literal today; the repo's existing pattern is a `Literal` field plus `Field(discriminator=...)` in `services/agent/events/envelope.py:55-107`. Match it.
